newsitem.title: SPAIN: Cofir's NH buy could pave way for placing.
newsitem.headline: Cofir's NH buy could pave way for placing.

text.p: Spanish investment firm Cofir's decision to increase its stake in NH Hotels to 100 percent could be aimed at reducing diversification and will probably lead to a stock market placing for NH shares, according to analysts.
"Concentrating on its better businesses, wine and hotels, is good news for Cofir shareholders", said Alejandro Ruira of AB Asesores.
Cofir agreed on Tuesday to buy the stake in NH Hotels that it did not already own from chairman Antonio Catalan's Grupo Catalan, raising its holding from 66.6 percent to 100 percent.
In exchange Grupo Catalan will receive real estate from the chain, which will remain managed by NH Hotels.
Another analyst said there appeared to be an agreement between NH and Cofir to place the hotel chain on the stock market, a possibility which had recently been mentioned.
"Cofir may plan to place a portion of NH on the stock market, but there was no agreement. Cofir knows, however, that it is one of its leading assets", said an analyst who wished to remain anonymous.
Analysts agreed that Catalan's eventual withdrawal from NH Hotels was negative for the company, which he has guided to strong growth with over 70 hotels.

"I believe that there was a difference between the managers of Cofir and NH concerning a stock market placement and an exchange of shares, which would have turned Catalan into the strongman in Cofir", said an analyst.
In addition to the NH stake, Cofir's managers plan to concentrate their investments in Bodegas Barberana, of which it owns 55 percent.
Cofir also owns a stake of about 49 percent in the luxury real estate firm Sotogrande, which it could be planning to sell, analysts said.

"The news was a surprise given that an exchange of shares had been discussed between the two companies, which would have made Catalan an important Cofir shareholder", said Juan Cueto, an analyst at Ibersecurities.
A Cofir spokesman told Reuters that the company would not be in a position to give any details about the deal for another 15 days.
Experts value NH Hoteles at between 32 billion and 40 billion pesetas.
